title: Version-shaped passes queue in version order
lead: A version-shaped pass key ranks by its version in `list`, `next` and the TUI queue, declared or not, so a later release's slices never queue before an earlier release's.
findings_note: 2026-10-15: after retargeting, list put v1.13 s278 above v1.12 s298; graph.ranked_order ranks only declared passes, and v1.7+ are undeclared
boundary: **Not in this slice:** render order (already by version); `prose add-pass` or `set --pass` hints for undeclared keys; parsing pre-release keys such as `v1.2-rc1` (they stay non-version keys, as in render); `--sort score` and `--sort effort`, which stay flat.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
On 2026-10-15 the owner moved the open v1.11 items into v1.12 (relay) and v1.13 (TUI). `slicer list` then put s278 (v1.13, score 22) second, above s298 (v1.12, score 22), and s280 (v1.13) above s299 and s301 (v1.12).

The cause is `graph.ranked_order` (`src/slicer/graph.py:170`). It ranks a pass by its position in `index.passes`, the declared passes, and gives every undeclared key the same rank, `len(passes)`, so they fall back to score. This roadmap declares v1 to v1.6 and `later`; every pass from v1.7 on is undeclared, so they all tie, and the declared `later` ranks ahead of all of them.

This is documented, not accidental: `docs/commands.md` (the `list` row) says "Pass labels are not parsed as versions: declare earlier releases before later releases and put a deferred pass last." The rule asks every project to `prose add-pass` each release in order, and `set --pass` on a new key gives no hint that it was not declared. The renderer already parses versions (`render._version_parts`, `src/slicer/render.py:291`) and shows version-shaped keys newest first, so the queue and the roadmap disagree about the same keys.

The owner asked that a slice targeting a later version never schedule before one targeting a lower version.

sections.heading: Files
Failing tests
sections.body:
- `test_List_UndeclaredVersionPasses_RankByVersion`: undeclared v1.13 with a higher score and undeclared v1.12 with a lower one; `list --json` puts the v1.12 item first, and `next` returns it.
- `test_List_VersionPasses_IgnoreDeclarationOrder`: v1.13 declared before v1.12; the v1.12 item still ranks first.
- `test_List_NonVersionPass_FollowsVersions`: a declared `later` declared before an undeclared v1.12; the v1.12 item ranks first, `later` after.
- `test_List_VersionPasses_NumericNotLexical`: v1.10 ranks after v1.2, and `v1` before `v1.1`.
- `test_Ranking_VersionPasses_AscendingReverses`: ascending puts the later version first.
- `test_Tui_Queue_VersionPassesMatchList`: the TUI queue order equals `list`'s.
- Existing `test_List_DeclaredReleases_OverrideOpposingScoresInEveryProfile` and `test_List_CustomPasses_MergeEmptyByScoreAndKeepUnknownAfterDeclared` still pass, or are updated only where their keys are version-shaped and the old rule is what they pinned (say which in the handoff note).

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the tests and watch them go red against today's `ranked_order`.
2. Lift `_version_parts` to the shared place and rank named keys as Files says.
3. Reword the four docs and add the CHANGELOG entry; mutation-check the new tests (swap the version sort direction, drop the version branch).

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `python3.12 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests` passes.
- In this repo, `slicer list` shows every v1.12 item before every v1.13 item within each readiness group.
- `slicer check` passes and render output is byte-identical (`git diff --stat .slicer/render/` is empty after `slicer render`).

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch; the owner lands it.
